jobs.description: Electronic Arts creates next-level entertainment experiences that inspire players and fans around the world. Here, everyone is part of the story. Part of a community that connects across the globe. A place where creativity thrives, new perspectives are invited, and ideas matter. A team where everyone makes play happen. We Are EA At Electronic Arts, we create experiences that inspire players and communities around the world. Making great games is challenging, and it takes creative, curious, and passionate people working together to make those experiences possible. EA Digital Platform : Gameplay Services The EA Digital Platform provides shared technology and services that help game teams tap into the power of the global EA ecosystem. By building reusable capabilities that can be integrated across games, we enable our studios to focus on what they do best, creating incredible experiences for players. Within Gameplay Services, we build and operate online capabilities used across EA games, including Stats & Leaderboards . The Challenge Ahead Stats & Leaderboards touches player experiences across EA's portfolio. Our technology helps games capture player statistics, track progress and accomplishments, compare players and friends, and power leaderboard experiences. Behind those experiences are highly available, distributed backend systems designed to process and serve player data at scale. As a Software Engineer Intern , you'll work alongside experienced engineers to build and improve these production services. You'll get hands-on experience solving real engineering problems while contributing to software that improves player experiences across EA games. You will report to a Technical Director on the team. What You'll Do Design and implement backend features using Java and Spring Boot . Build and evolve service interfaces using gRPC and Protocol Buffers . Work with PostgreSQL and Redis to store, retrieve, and process player statistics and leaderboard data. Develop and run services in a Kubernetes-based environment. Write production-quality code along with unit and integration tests. Investigate and debug issues using logs, metrics, traces, and other observability tools. Learn how we design and optimize distributed systems for performance, scalability, reliability, and availability . Participate in code reviews and technical design discussions with experienced engineers. Collaborate with engineers across Gameplay Services and EA game teams. Participate in the team's sprint cycle, including stand-ups, sprint planning, backlog refinement, demos, and retrospectives. Own a well-scoped engineering project or feature from design and implementation through testing and delivery. What We're Looking For Pursuing a bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering , or a related technical field. Programming experience with Java and an understanding of object-oriented programming. Understanding of core computer science concepts including data structures, algorithms, concurrency, and databases . Curiosity about how large-scale systems work. A player- and customer-focused mindset—you think about how the technology you build ultimately affects the people using it. Exposure to any of the following: Spring / Spring Boot gRPC and Protocol Buffers PostgreSQL or other relational databases Redis or other caching technologies Docker and Kubernetes Microservices or distributed systems Cloud technologies Automated testing and CI/CD Performance testing, profiling, or optimization What You'll Learn You'll experience the full software development lifecycle on a production engineering team—from understanding requirements and participating in technical design to implementation, testing, deployment, monitoring, and iteration. You'll gain practical experience with Java, Spring Boot, gRPC, PostgreSQL, Redis, and Kubernetes while learning how distributed backend services are built and operated at EA scale. Through mentorship, code reviews, design discussions, and hands-on development, you'll learn from experienced engineers while gradually taking greater ownership of your work. Most importantly, you'll ship meaningful software that contributes to player experiences across EA's games. You must be available for a full-time paid internship in the summer of 2026. At this time, we are considering Bachelor's students who will be enrolled in an accredited degree program in the summer of 2027, slated to graduate no earlier than December 2027 . Applicants must be legally authorized to work in Canada on a full-time basis during the 16-week internship. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position. Please ensure that your graduation date is visible on your resume. Pay Transparency - North America * British Columbia (depending on location e.g. Vancouver vs. Victoria) *$65,000 - $70,000 CAD Pay is just one part of the overall compensation at EA. About Electronic Arts We’re proud to have an extensive portfolio of games and experiences, locations around the world, and opportunities across EA. We value adaptability, resilience, creativity, and curiosity. From leadership that brings out your potential, to creating space for learning and experimenting, we empower you to do great work and pursue opportunities for growth. We adopt a holistic approach to our benefits programs, emphasizing physical, emotional, financial, career, and community wellness to support a balanced life. Our packages are tailored to meet local needs and may include healthcare coverage, mental well-being support, retirement savings, paid time off, family leaves, complimentary games, and more. We nurture environments where our teams can always bring their best to what they do. Electronic Arts is an equal opportunity employer. Why Sony Interactive Entertainment?
Sony Interactive Entertainment isn’t just the Best Place to Play — it’s also the Best Place to Work. Sony Interactive Entertainment (SIE) is the company behind the PlayStation brand. As a subsidiary of Sony Group Corporation, we’re part of a proud legacy of innovation and excellence. SIE is a dynamic technology company, delivering cutting-edge hardware and network services to more than 100 million people and an entertainment leader, home to some of the most beloved and recognizable intellectual properties (IP) in the world. Our role at SIE is to create and nurture the experiences under the PlayStation brand, a name synonymous with entertainment excellence and creativity.
Role overview:
The PlayStation Store is a multibillion-dollar global digital commerce platform at the center of how players discover, buy, and enjoy content - and this role turns commercial priorities into a coherent, executable trading plan.
As the
Trading Planning Lead
, you will build the Store's integrated trading plan, joining launches, promotions, pricing, catalogue, lifecycle, and real-world moments into a clear roadmap with defined outcomes, owners, and dependencies.
This individual-contributor role reports to the Senior Manager, Planning & Proposition and works across Trading Optimisation, Catalogue Planning, Promotions & Experimentation, Finance, Monetisation, , Merchandising & Editorial, Insights & Analytics, and regional teams. You will provide a trusted source of truth for priorities, decisions, and execution readiness.
You will work closely with the Trading Performance Lead, connecting performance opportunities and risks into forward looking plans, spot conflicts and risks early to escalate through trading governance, and improve the tools and governance that help global teams deliver together.
What you’ll be doing:
Build the integrated 360 trading plan
Convert commercial strategy, title roadmaps, promotions, pricing actions, lifecycle activity, and major events into an outcome-focused weekly, monthly, and quarterly Store plan.
Run the trading planning rhythm
Coordinate all planning inputs and materials for weekly, monthly, and quarterly reviews; maintain decisions, actions, owners, and due dates; track follow-through and escalate blockers to closure.
Maintain the planning source of truth
Keep the central planning sheet, master calendar, priority sheets, and understand dependencies so teams can plan capacity and execute from consistent information.
Connect performance to future plans
Partner with the Trading Performance Lead, Insights & Analytics and Finance to surface performance drivers, risks, and trends; feed actuals and post-mortem learning into forecast assumptions, prioritisation, and the next trading cycle.
Drive prioritisation and trade-offs
Identify collisions across launches, promotions, real-world events, and customer journeys; assess commercial impact and readiness; present clear options and recommendations to Store leaders.
Coordinate delivery and improve ways of working
Align Trading, Catalogue Planning, Merchandising, Pricing, LTV, Monetisation, Marketing, Store Build, and regional teams; improve intake, SLAs, automation, and governance to reduce rework and increase speed.
What we’re looking for:
A minimum of 8+ years of experience in trading, commercial planning, programme management, ecommerce, or business operations within a fast-paced, customer-facing environment.
Practical experience building integrated plans and running weekly, monthly, and quarterly trading or commercial planning cycles.
Strong commercial and analytical capability, with confidence using revenue, conversion, engagement, margin, and customer KPIs to prioritise work and recommend action.
Excellent programme-management discipline, including management of milestones, owners, dependencies, risks, action logs, and planning tools.
Proven cross-functional leadership and ability to influence stakeholders across global and local teams without relying on formal authority.
Clear written, verbal, and visual communication, with the ability to turn complex inputs into concise plans and decision-ready trading materials.
A resilient, adaptable, and outcome-focused mindset, with strong ownership, attention to detail, and sound judgement under pressure.

Experience in digital commerce, games, media, marketplaces, or another high-volume content or subscription environment.
Working knowledge of promotions, pricing, merchandising, catalogue planning, and content lifecycle activity.
Experience partnering with Finance on forecasting, budgeting, and performance-to-plan reviews.
Hands-on experience with experimentation, post-mortems, and data-led decision-making in a trading environment.

Product Partnerships sits within the Enterprise Sales organization and is responsible for the strategic vision, acquisition, management, and growth of DoorDash’s partnerships with all the merchant, restaurant technology, and advertiser technology providers. This executive leads performance marketing, market investment, and growth planning for New, Used, We Buy Your Car, and After-Sales, with direct accountability for delivering qualified opportunity volume and at an efficient cost per sale/purchase. The role connects national scale with regional, market, and store priorities and partners closely with business line leaders, Field Marketing, Brand, Customer Relationship Management, Digital Product, Analytics, Finance, Operations, original equipment manufacturers, and agency partners to drive measurable growth, market share, and investment efficiency. 1. Enterprise Growth and Media Strategy • Set the enterprise growth and full-funnel media strategy to generate qualified demand, improve market share, support profitable sales, and strengthen customer retention. • Lead annual, quarterly, and monthly media planning across national, regional, market, and store levels, balancing enterprise scale with local relevance and original equipment manufacturer requirements. • Allocate investment across brand and performance channels using business objectives, market opportunity, inventory, customer demand, and marginal-return insights. • Create clear decision frameworks for channel mix, audience strategy, geographic prioritization, pacing, optimization, and test-and-learn activity. • Own the enterprise plan for paid demand and communicate expected opportunity volume, efficiency, and sales contribution by line of business. 2. Line of Business Growth Plans • Lead growth and media plans for New, Used, We Buy Your Car, and After-Sales, translating revenue, share, inventory, margin, and customer objectives into actionable demand plans. • Partner with each line of business to define target audiences, offers, messaging, media roles, customer journeys, and performance expectations. • Identify enterprise and cross-line-of-business opportunities that increase customer lifetime value and position AutoNation as the preferred partner across the full automotive ownership journey. • Bring competitive, customer, market, and performance insights forward to shape business decisions and near-term actions. 3. Performance Marketing and Demand Delivery • Lead performance marketing across paid search, paid social, video, display, programmatic, audio, and other demand channels, ensuring investment is aligned to the highest-value opportunities. • Establish performance goals, measurement standards, reporting cadences, and clear accountability across channels and lines of business. • Own marketing performance against committed opportunity volume and cost per sale, and initiate corrective action when performance is off plan. • Evaluate opportunity quality, conversion, sales, market share, cost per opportunity, cost per sale, incremental lift, and return on investment to determine where action is required. • Partner with Analytics and Finance to advance attribution, incrementality testing, forecasting, audience measurement, and investment governance. • Lead regular performance reviews and translate insights into specific actions while managing major platform and budget changes with appropriate testing discipline. 4. Market Investment and Field Partnership • Own the framework for allocating and recalibrating media investment across regions, markets, and stores based on demand, competitive position, inventory, performance, and growth opportunity. • Partner with Field Marketing, regional and market leaders, and stores to connect enterprise strategy with local business conditions and sales priorities. • Develop a scalable enterprise, regional, market, and store media model that improves efficiency while maintaining meaningful local support. • Create transparent market- and store-level investment views, performance diagnostics, and recalibration processes that distinguish marketing opportunity from operational conversion needs. • Ensure plans reflect inventory availability, competitive conditions, merchandising, close-rate performance, and local market opportunity. 5. Social Media and Third Party Media Leadership • Own the enterprise social media strategy across paid, organic, platform, content distribution, community, and reputation considerations in partnership with Brand and Corporate Communications. • Lead the strategy and governance for third-party marketplaces, lead providers, publishers, and media partnerships, including investment, quality standards, testing, and performance accountability. • Develop first-party data, audience, personalization, and retargeting strategies that strengthen acquisition and retention across channels. • Evaluate emerging platforms, partners, and capabilities and scale those that demonstrate measurable business value. 6. Agency Performance and Commercial Governance • Lead agency-of-record and key partner relationships, setting strategic direction, operating expectations, scopes of work, performance standards, and executive governance. • Hold agencies accountable for opportunity delivery, cost-per-sale improvement, media quality, optimization speed, innovation, and transparent reporting. • Partner with Procurement, Finance, and Legal to negotiate agreements and ensure investments, fees, incentives, data rights, and deliverables are transparent and competitive. • Build productive partnerships with original equipment manufacturers and certified providers to maximize co-op eligibility, data access, and shared learning while protecting AutoNation’s enterprise strategy. • Hold internal and external teams accountable for high-quality planning, execution, optimization, reporting, and innovation. 7. Team Leadership and Enterprise Influence • Build, lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team with clear roles, priorities, performance expectations, and career development plans. • Influence senior leaders across Marketing, Sales, Operations, Finance, Technology, and the Field through concise, data-led recommendations and clear tradeoffs. • Create an operating culture of urgency, curiosity, collaboration, disciplined experimentation, and accountability for business outcomes. Company Expectations • Demonstrate behaviors consistent with the Company’s Vision, Mission, and Values in all interactions with customers, co-workers, and suppliers. • Adhere to all company policies, procedures, and safety standards. Qualifications • Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Business, Communications, Economics, Analytics, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience. Master’s degree preferred. • Twelve or more years of progressive marketing experience, including significant leadership of integrated media, performance marketing, or enterprise growth strategy for a complex, multi-location consumer business. • Seven or more years of people leadership experience, with success building teams, developing talent, and leading through influence in a matrixed organization. • Demonstrated ownership of large, multi-channel media investments spanning brand and performance channels, including paid search, paid and organic social, video, audio, display, programmatic, and third-party media. • Proven ability to translate enterprise and line-of-business objectives into integrated plans that deliver measurable demand, revenue, market-share, efficiency, and customer outcomes. • Strong command of marketing measurement, financial stewardship, incrementality, attribution, experimentation, forecasting, and executive performance reporting. • Experience leading agencies, platforms, publishers, marketplaces, and complex commercial partnerships. Automotive, retail, franchise, dealer, or other distributed-location experience preferred. • Exceptional executive communication, judgment, negotiation, change leadership, and cross-functional partnership skills. • Must meet company requirements for employment. • Valid in-state driver’s license and an acceptable, safe driving record maintained throughout employment. Leadership Profile Enterprise strategist. Connects brand, demand generation, customer experience, and commercial priorities into a coherent growth agenda. Performance-oriented operator. Uses data to identify the highest-value opportunities, act with appropriate speed, and hold teams accountable for results. Influential partner. Builds trust across enterprise and field teams and creates alignment among stakeholders with different priorities. Customer-centered leader. Keeps the customer journey and long-term relationship at the center of media, channel, and investment decisions. Talent builder. Creates clarity, develops strong leaders, and builds an inclusive, high-accountability team culture. The intent of this job description is to provide a representative summary of the major duties and responsibilities performed by incumbents of this job. Incumbents may be requested to perform job-related tasks other than those specifically presented. ㅤ $225,000.00 - $375,000.00 ㅤ Exciting Benefits and Perks Await You: Competitive compensation and 401k matching Enjoy a healthy work-life balance with insurance plans (health, dental, vision) and maternity benefits. Associate purchase and discount programs for new and pre-owned vehicles, services, parts, collision, accessories, and AutoGear Access amazing deals and discounts through YouDecide, a website with offers from top providers and retailers Join our DRVPNK mission to raise and donate millions of dollars to cancer research and treatment, partnering with cancer charities nationwide AutoNation is one of the largest automotive retailers in the United States, offering innovative products, exceptional services, and comprehensive solutions, empowering our customers to make the best decisions for their needs. With a network of dealerships nationwide strengthened by a recognized brand, we offer a wide variety of new and used vehicles, customer financing, parts, and provide expert maintenance and repair services. Through DRV PNK, we have raised over $40 million for cancer-related causes, demonstrating our commitment to making a positive difference in the lives of our Associates, Customers, and the communities we serve. AutoNation is committed to creating a diverse, equitable, and inclusive environment in our workplace and the services we provide. We welcome candidates from all backgrounds who are passionate about making a positive impact. Even if you do not meet every requirement, we encourage you to apply. Join our team and help us foster a culture of belonging while contributing to our revolutionary work in the automotive industry. We value innovation, teamwork, and a commitment to making a positive impact in the world.
